newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Brabeck approved as new Nestle CEO.
newsitem.headline: Brabeck approved as new Nestle CEO.

text.p: Nestle SA shareholders endorsed Peter Brabeck as new chief executive of the world's biggest food group by electing him to the board of directors.
Brabeck, a 52-year-old Austrian, replaces Helmut Maucher, who built Nestle into a global powerhouse and who will continue to play an active role as chairman.
Brabeck has said in the past he did not plan big strategic changes at Nestle, whose marketing strategy he has largely shaped for the past five years.
Brabeck has made his career at Nestle, rising from driving an ice cream truck to its top executive post.
He has extensive experience in Latin America and headed the culinary products division at headquarters in Vevey from 1987 to 1991.
Greenpeace demonstrators gathered outside the annual meeting to urge shareholders to reject genetic engineering of foods.
Brabeck defended genetically altered products, which he said would help feed a growing world population and cut the overuse of fertilisers and chemicals.
"Products that are improved by genetic technology will be even safer than products today," he said.
He added Nestle management would continue to decide on a country by country basis whether to introduce such products.
"Each market will decide for itself," he said.
In response to a shareholder's question, Brabeck said Nestle was paying close attention to the use of infant formula in developing countries.
He pledged the company would fully implement the World Health Organisation code on the subject, and said he hoped to work with the company's critics to resolve the controversial issue.
